title: OpenAI Takes on Microsoft With ChatGPT's Own Office Suite at DevDay
excerpt: At DevDay in San Francisco, OpenAI unveiled Space, Pages, and collaborative slides — workplace tools that put the ChatGPT maker in direct competition with Microsoft 365 and Google Workspace.
body:
• At its DevDay developer conference in San Francisco on September 29, 2026, OpenAI announced Space, a shared workspace inside ChatGPT, alongside Pages, a word processor, and collaborative slides.
  • Space brings co-workers, files, pages, and OpenAI's new Dots agent personas together; users can give pages live instructions, such as checking a team channel and updating itself with what it finds.
  • The features compete directly with Microsoft Word, PowerPoint, and Google Docs — even as Microsoft remains OpenAI's largest backer and the model supplier behind Copilot.
  • Rollout: Space and Pages are going to eligible ChatGPT Pro, Business, and Enterprise accounts first; collaborative slides arrive in the coming weeks; on mobile, pages can be found, read, and shared, with creation and editing on web and desktop.

OpenAI has spent years as Microsoft's closest partner in artificial intelligence. At its DevDay developer conference in San Francisco on Tuesday, the AI lab unveiled a set of ChatGPT features that put it squarely in its biggest backer's territory: workplace software.

The company announced Space, a shared workspace inside ChatGPT where co-workers collaborate with the chatbot and with Dots, OpenAI's newly launched AI agent personas that carry out tasks on a user's behalf. It also introduced Pages, a word processor, and collaborative slides — tools that closely mirror the core components of Microsoft 365 and Google Workspace.

"Your pages and files all live together in Space, like they would in a drive. But spaces feel alive."

— Sam Altman, CEO, OpenAI

Context & Background

Space is the centerpiece. Files and pages live together inside a shared environment, similar to a drive, but users can give individual pages specific instructions — Altman demonstrated telling a page to check a team channel and update itself with what it found. Dots, the agent personas introduced alongside Space, operate within that environment carrying out tasks on behalf of users rather than sitting in a separate chatbot window.

https://x.com/derleomartin/status/2106408841198071859

Pages is OpenAI's answer to Google Docs and Microsoft Word: "a new type of document, built for human and agent collaboration." Users can write, research, generate charts, create images, or visualize information inside it, according to the company. Collaborative slides extend the same concept to presentations — users generate decks by describing them in conversation with ChatGPT, after which co-workers and agents can edit them, leave comments, and iterate. Slides are not yet available but will roll out in the coming weeks, an OpenAI representative said.

The move follows another encroachment: in September, OpenAI launched a ChatGPT add-in for Microsoft Word itself, available across every ChatGPT plan including Free, with the same integration extended to PowerPoint and Excel. That puts a ChatGPT-branded sidebar directly inside the products where Microsoft sells its own Copilot assistant.

Impact & Analysis

The partnership math is getting complicated. Microsoft has invested billions in OpenAI and builds its own Copilot products on top of OpenAI's models. Now OpenAI is building tools that compete for the same enterprise software budgets — word processing, presentations, and team collaboration — the categories that made Microsoft the most valuable software company in the world.

The bet is that AI-native documents are fundamentally different from the documents Word and Google Docs were designed for. A page that can be instructed to monitor a team channel and rewrite itself is not a file; it is a small, persistent worker. If enterprises accept that framing, the competitive question shifts from which company has the best editor to which has the best agents — and OpenAI is now building both the editor and the agents.

Microsoft, for its part, has spent the past year racing to become more like OpenAI, releasing a steady stream of AI products as the software industry reorients around the new landscape. Google's Workspace and Salesforce's productivity offerings face the same pressure from the other side of the partnership line.

Diaspora Angle

For the large Indian diaspora workforce in American technology — engineers, product managers, and startup founders for whom ChatGPT is already embedded in daily work — the change is practical: the documents and decks where distributed teams actually collaborate are becoming the place where AI agents operate, not a chat window off to the side.

What's Next

Execution now matters more than announcements. Slides must ship on schedule and land well with enterprise users; Dots must prove themselves as reliable agents inside real workflows, including integrations with Slack and Microsoft Teams that OpenAI has signaled. Pricing and availability beyond paid tiers remain open questions — Space is currently limited to eligible Pro, Business, and Enterprise accounts.

The deeper question is how Microsoft responds. The two companies are simultaneously the industry's closest allies and increasingly direct competitors for the future of office software. DevDay made clear that OpenAI intends to compete as much as collaborate.
